papers.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
papers.summary: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

papers.title: Stochastic Port-Hamiltonian Gaussian Processes for Learning from Noisy Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.summary: Learning predictive models for dynamics is difficult because observations are often sparse and noisy, while the underlying dynamics evolve on nonlinear configuration manifolds and are affected by environmental dissipation and stochastic disturbances. Standard neural dynamics models can fit short-term trajectories but often violate physical structure, accumulate error over long horizons, or rely on parameterizations that introduce singularities such as gimbal lock. We introduce LieSPHGP, a stochastic Gaussian-process framework for learning rigid body dynamics with port-Hamiltonian structure and stability-aware robustness. LieSPHGP represents motion on Lie groups and Lie algebras, enabling coordinate-consistent optimization without singular parameterizations. Learned mass, potential energy, dissipation, and control components retain physical roles and a separate diffusion term represents stochastic forcing. Each component is modeled by Matérn kernel Gaussian processes which capture uncertainty induced by noisy observations. To improve physical validity, Lie group exponential map updates preserve rotational constraints, while positive-definite damping ensures nonnegative deterministic energy dissipation. The implicit-explicit integrator additionally provides unconditional stability for the frozen linear damping subsystem. The resulting model learns predictive dynamics that are robust to noise, respect rigid body geometry, and capture both intrinsic motion and environmental dissipation. Experiments on various noisy rigid body benchmarks show improved prediction accuracy, stronger long-horizon stability, and better satisfaction of manifold constraints compared with neural dynamics baselines. Code, data and interactive results are available on the project website: https://thribhuvanrapolu.github.io/liesphgp/

papers.title: Typed Edge-Tensor Non-Reciprocal Port-Hamiltonian Deliberation for Counterfactual Open-World Deductive Reasoning
papers.summary: Scaling test-time computation in continuous latent spaces offers an attractive alternative to verbose token-by-token generation for multi-step deductive reasoning. However, unregularized recurrent latent updates suffer from a deliberation drift cliff when rolled out beyond training horizons, while strictly energy-conserving or symmetric message-passing dynamics cannot break parent-to-child causal symmetry or suppress cyclic modus-ponens amplification on cyclic distraction graphs. We introduce Typed Edge-Tensor Non-Reciprocal Port-Hamiltonian Deliberation (TE-BPHD), a neuro-symbolic continuous-time latent reasoning architecture that couples skew-symmetric port-Hamiltonian conservation with relation-typed non-reciprocal directional transport and monotone dissipative damping on a semantic entity-state manifold. We prove (i) unconditional input-to-state stability and exponential contraction of autonomous rollouts across arbitrary inference depths without external norm projection, (ii) strict directional DAG reachability separation over symmetric message passing, and (iii) exact cycle-suppression margins under finite cyclic horn perturbations. Across counterfactual open-world deductive benchmarks (PrOntoQA-OOD up to depth 15, ProofWriter-OWA Cyclic at depths 5-10, FOLIO-Symbolic, and Cluttr-Relational), TE-BPHD eliminates the deep-horizon drift cliff, improves depth-10 cyclic reasoning accuracy to 90.0% (+/- 0.8%) over symmetric port-Hamiltonian and standard Transformer baselines, and supports zero-retraining adaptive Lyapunov halting that reduces average solver evaluations by 44% with negligible accuracy loss.

papers.title: Port-Hamiltonian Systems Beyond Joules: A Review of Unexpected Application Domains
papers.summary: The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. Over the past fifteen years it has spread to chemistry, cell biology, fusion plasmas, musical instruments, district heating, electricity markets, macroeconomics, predator-prey ecology, optimization algorithms and neural-network training. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.

papers.title: Instantaneous control for stabilization of interacting particle systems: convergence rates and dominant frequencies
papers.summary: We study a class of Cucker-Smale-type systems with a binary interaction potential subject to an external control input. We apply an instantaneous rolling horizon control (IRHC) feedback to address two different control problems: full set-point stabilization of a spatial configuration with zero velocity and stabilization of the center of mass at a desired position with zero mean velocity using a single external agent. The IRHC feedback has been shown to preserve the port-Hamiltonian structure of the corresponding open-loop systems. We analyze how the control parameters and the time discretization affect convergence rates and oscillation frequencies and compare the IRHC feedback with the corresponding IDA-PBC feedback obtained by omitting an additional correction term. For the reduced center of mass dynamics, we derive explicit predictions for continuous- and discrete-time spectral decay rates and oscillation frequencies and verify these predictions numerically. For the full nonlinear particle system, the controller comparison is done by numerical experiments.

papers.title: PH-Symb : Sparse symbolic identification of nonlinear port-Hamiltonian systems using Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
papers.summary: The paper introduces PH-Symb, a novel symbolic structure-preserving identification method, that combines Kolmogorov Arnold networks and sparse regression to build explicit port-Hamiltonian (pH) models from data. Unlike other Machine Learning or neural pH approaches, PH-Symb recovers physically interpretable and explicit-symbolic components and enforces pH structure by construction. It also introduces a new normalization method that preserves the pH structure. It allows handling both identification from input-state-output (ISO) data and input-output (IO) data, and applications show it delivers interpretable models and lower errors than neural baselines on synthetic and real-world systems.

papers.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
papers.summary: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

papers.title: Koopman Generator Decomposition for Port-Hamiltonian Systems
papers.summary: Port-Hamiltonian energy balance and Koopman approximation describe different aspects of nonlinear dynamics. This paper distinguishes exact observable identities, measure-dependent Galerkin projections, constrained surrogate identification, and certification of a controller on the nonlinear plant. Conservative weak skewness requires compatible measure and boundary conditions. Dissipative positivity belongs to the metric bracket; it does not generally make the projected first-order dissipative derivation positive. We give an explicit fixed-metric compatibility condition and a constant--Hamiltonian dictionary obstruction, and state the assumptions under which surrogate certificates imply plant bounds. A reproduced pendulum experiment illustrates the practical gap: its learned controller admits an exact shaped-energy certificate on the nonlinear plant, although its fitted quadratic storage is not a plant Lyapunov function and its archived residual-norm diagnostic is uninformative. These conclusions use the specified plant structure; they are not generic finite-data guarantees. The bracket, projection, and Lyapunov arguments are positioned relative to existing structured identification and residual-aware control methods.

papers.title: Descriptor representations of geometric port-Hamiltonian systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.summary: We establish conversions in both directions between geometric and descriptor representations of linear port-Hamiltonian systems on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For the geometric-to-descriptor conversion, we represent the possibly multivalued inverse Dirac relation by a skew-adjoint operator on enlarged Hilbert spaces, retaining the original operator-domain restrictions. The construction accommodates internal and external ports. We show that the conversions preserve trajectories and the power balance. An incompressible Kelvin--Voigt solid illustrates the results.

papers.title: Discovering Phase Space Structure in Learned Hamiltonian Systems
papers.summary: Mechanics-inspired neural networks provide physically structured models of dynamical systems, but typically assume access to the coordinates in which the underlying dynamics are expressed. While recent generative approaches relax this assumption, they remain limited in their ability to jointly model different dynamical regimes and discover interpretable latent structure. We introduce Structured Phase Space GAN (SPS-GAN), a conditional generative framework that learns mechanical dynamics and discovers latent phase-space structure from Cartesian trajectories or video observations. We achieve this by combining adversarial generation with port-Hamiltonian latent dynamics and extending cyclic-coordinate regularization to account for dissipation and forcing. This formulation supports conservative, dissipative, and forced systems while encouraging compact latent representations from which active degrees of freedom can be identified. Experiments on simulated and real-world systems demonstrate improved trajectory accuracy and video generation quality over competitive baselines, while identifying active latent dimensions consistent with the expected effective degrees of freedom and recovering physically interpretable coordinates across observation modalities and dynamical regimes.

papers.title: Comparing model representations and fitting methods for port-Hamiltonian system identification
papers.summary: Port-Hamiltonian models describe physical systems by separating stored energy, dissipation and external inputs. Learning such models from data requires a choice of representation and fitting method. We compare using neural networks, analytic expressions and combinations of the two for representing the different components of the port-Hamiltonian system, and compare fitting the models with gradient-based optimisation or sparse regression. Testing on simulations of mechanical and electrical systems, with and without added noise, we present prediction accuracy and computational cost of the different approaches.

papers.title: Adaptive data-driven reduced-order models for reciprocal MIMO port-Hamiltonian dynamical systems
papers.summary: Port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems provide a general framework for modeling a broad class of physical dynamical systems, including systems with dissipation. Constructing accurate and robust data-driven reduced-order models for general pH systems is challenging. In this work, we focus on an important subclass of pH systems satisfying reciprocity, a property arising naturally in a variety of models. Rather than seeking to preserve the full pH structure, we exploit the additional symmetry provided by reciprocity to develop an efficient data-driven reduced-order modeling approach. We show that every minimal realization of a reciprocal system is self-adjoint with respect to a generally indefinite inner product and can, up to a similarity transformation preserving the pH structure, be represented in a Krein space with a signature inner product. This observation motivates a Galerkin projection onto a tangential rational Krylov subspace with respect to the corresponding indefinite inner product. Although the resulting projection involves full-order state solutions and the unknown inner product, we show that its reduced mass and stiffness matrices can be constructed directly from transfer-function data through a Loewner formulation. We then propose a greedy data-driven procedure that adaptively selects both interpolation frequencies and tangential directions. At every iteration, the frequency is chosen according to the largest transfer-function approximation error, while the tangential direction is selected from a dominant singular direction of the corresponding matrix-valued residual. Numerical experiments for wave propagation in lossy media demonstrate improved approximation efficiency compared with block adaptive interpolation. We further apply the method to spectral mass gauging of a three-dimensional propellant tank to provide an accurate estimate of the tank volume through Weyl's law.

papers.title: L2-L2-gain bounds for quadratic output systems
papers.summary: We derive an explicit bound for the L2-L2-gain of linear time-invariant systems whose output is a quadratic function of the state and the input. Such systems appear naturally in many areas, for example for port-Hamiltonian systems, optimal-control, and stochastic problems. In case the output is purely quadratic in the state, the bound is determined by the supremum over $ω\in\mathbb R$ of the L2-norms of the bivariate transfer function restricted to the anti-diagonals $\{(s,\, iω-s)\mid s\in i\mathbb R\}$ of the frequency domain $i\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R $. Further, we show how the bound can be computed by solving linear matrix equations. This result provides a practical tool for assessing and reducing quadratic-output models.

papers.title: Exponential stability of port-Hamiltonian systems with unstructured, measurable Hamiltonian densities
papers.summary: For first-order port-Hamiltonian systems in the dissipative setting considered here, we characterise exponential stability without any further regularity or block-structure assumption on the Hamiltonian density, thus closing a gap persisting in the literature. The proof requires revisiting the computation of the adjoint generator of the port-Hamiltonian semigroup. Finally, we provide both examples and non-examples showcasing the inconclusiveness of known conditions on the Hamiltonian densities necessary for the application of characterisation results in the literature.

papers.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
papers.summary: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.

papers.title: On the Stability Analysis of Infinite-Dimensional Port-Hamiltonian Systems Within the Variational Framework
papers.summary: This paper addresses the stability analysis of a class of linear infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems formulated within the variational framework. We derive verifiable conditions for the equivalence of the Hamiltonian-induced energy norm and the natural state-space norm, as well as for the generation of a contraction semigroup by the associated system operator. The semigroup generation result is obtained by establishing dissipativity and verifying the required range condition. The proposed conditions simplify the functional-analytic stability analysis of this class of systems in a manner similar to established results for the Stokes-Dirac setting.

papers.title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
papers.summary: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

papers.title: Energy-Based Fault Detection and Isolation Framework for Flat Port-Hamiltonian Mechanical Systems
papers.summary: Fault diagnosis during regulated motion requires informative signals even when feedback attenuates tracking deviations. This paper develops an energy-based diagnostic framework that constructs mechanical port-power residuals without a dedicated dynamic observer. Spectral Hamiltonian Algebraic Power Evaluation (SHAPE) combines port-Hamiltonian variables and differential flatness to generate nominal power references from planned motion for fully actuated mechanical systems with collocated actuation. Subtracting these references from commanded effort multiplied by measured flow yields residuals whose final evaluation requires neither recursive observer updates nor measured-state dynamics calculations. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalograms and a shared-encoder convolutional neural network are used to distinguish nominal operation, actuator loss of effectiveness, anomalous friction, and vibration from complete trajectories. Evaluation uses a simulated six degree of freedom Kinova manipulator under model predictive control and fixed plant-model mismatch, with single faults at a specified joint. Across five training seeds and 3000 held-out test runs, SHAPE-CWT achieves a mean accuracy of 84.69 percent, versus 81.67 percent for torque residuals and 97.17 percent for the generalized momentum observer under common CWT processing. The respective sample standard deviations are 0.70, 0.70, and 0.37 percentage points. These results demonstrate useful fault-type discrimination from algebraic power residuals, while severity-excitation profiles and offline velocity perturbations reveal limits to their diagnostic capability.

papers.title: Port-Hamiltonian systems with energy and power ports
papers.summary: We extend the port-Hamiltonian framework defined with respect to a Lagrangian submanifold and a Dirac structure by augmenting the Lagrangian submanifold with the space of external variables. The new pair of conjugated variables is called energy port. We show that in the most general case, the extension describes constrained Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonian function depends on inputs.

papers.title: Mesh Field Theory: Port-Hamiltonian Formulation of Mesh-Based Physics
papers.summary: We present Mesh Field Theory (MeshFT) and its neural realization, MeshFT-Net: a structure-preserving framework for mesh-based continuum physics that cleanly separates the physics' topological structure from its metric structure. Imposing minimal physical principles (locality, permutation equivariance, orientation covariance, and energy balance/dissipation inequality), we prove a reduction theorem for mesh-based physics. Under these conditions, the physical dynamics admit a local factorization into a port-Hamiltonian form: the conservative interconnection is fixed uniquely by mesh topology, whereas metric effects enter only through constitutive relations and dissipation. This reduction clarifies what must be fixed and what should be learned, directly informing MeshFT-Net's design. Across evaluations on analytic and realistic datasets, physics-consistency tests, and out-of-distribution validation, MeshFT-Net achieves near-zero energy drift and strong physical fidelity (correct dispersion and momentum conservation) along with robust extrapolation and high data efficiency. By eliminating non-physical degrees of freedom and learning only metric-dependent structure, MeshFT provides a principled inductive bias for stable, faithful, and data-efficient learning-based physical simulation.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Spatial Kernels for Gaussian Process Distributed Port-Hamiltonian Systems
papers.summary: Gaussian process distributed port-Hamiltonian systems (GP-dPHS) enable data-driven modeling of distributed dynamical systems while preserving their physical structure. However, standard stationary kernels can be inefficient for spatially heterogeneous systems because they neither exploit known input invariances nor reflect structured spatial dependencies. We address this limitation with a structure-aware kernel design that removes irrelevant state coordinates and decouples state and spatial dependencies through a tensor-product covariance. This modular construction allows qualitative knowledge of spatial heterogeneity to be incorporated by selecting an appropriate spatial kernel without requiring an analytical description of the underlying profile. Numerical experiments on a nonlinear string with periodic, smoothly varying, and semi-piecewise stiffness profiles demonstrate that structural decoupling consistently improves reconstruction accuracy, while profile-matched spatial kernels yield substantially larger gains in force-field and trajectory reconstruction.

papers.title: Optimal energy conversion -- A port-Hamiltonian approach
papers.summary: This paper studies optimal energy conversion in port-Hamiltonian systems. We analyze state- and control-constrained finite-horizon optimal control problems that maximize energy conversion efficiencies. Under suitable reachability conditions, we show that the asymptotic optimal efficiencies exist and coincide with the corresponding optimal cyclic efficiencies. For a class of port-Hamiltonian systems describing coupled storage-conversion components, we further derive intrinsic limits on achievable energy conversion and establish a generalized Carnot-type efficiency bound. Our results provide an optimal-control framework connecting asymptotic optimal operation, cyclic operation, and fundamental efficiency limits for port-Hamiltonian systems.

papers.title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
papers.summary: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

papers.title: Mixed finite element discretization of intrinsic geometrically exact beams for multiplier-free multibody dynamics
papers.summary: The Reissner-Simo and Hodges models are two equivalent continuous descriptions of finite-strain beam dynamics. The Reissner-Simo formulation uses displacements and rotations, while the Hodges formulation is intrinsic and avoids both variables. Although equivalent in theory, the two approaches behave differently after discretization and offer distinct numerical advantages. In this work, we develop a structure-preserving discretization of the intrinsic planar beam formulation. Because the intrinsic equations involve linear differential operators, both kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions can be imposed naturally using mixed finite elements. The resulting formulation also enables multibody systems to be assembled without algebraic constraints, avoiding the stiff differential-algebraic equations typically introduced by kinematic constraints. We demonstrate the approach on different examples, also showing that closed kinematic loops can be modeled without algebraic constraints. The resulting interconnected systems retain a port-Hamiltonian structure, with all nonlinearities confined to the interconnection operator. This structure allows exact energy preservation when combined with implicit midpoint time integration. Furthermore the scheme appears to require less Newton iterations compared to existing energy preserving scheme.

papers.title: Well-Posedness and Strong Convergence of Infinite-Dimensional Port-Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Gradient Dynamics
papers.summary: We establish a functional-analytic framework that justifies the LaSalle convergence argument outlined in [van der Schaft, 2026] on port-Hamiltonian primal-dual gradient dynamics for finite-horizon optimal control of linear systems. In addition to strict convexity of the running cost as in \cite{vanderSchaft2026PDGJuly}, our analysis requires global Lipschitz continuity of the cost gradient. This ensures that the nonlinear gradient operator is well-defined and Lipschitz on the entire underlying space. We establish global well-posedness of the optimizer dynamics: every initial value determines a unique global mild solution, and the associated solution operators form a contraction semigroup. Similar to [Gernandtand Schaller, 2025], this is proved using tools from maximal monotone operator theory. Assuming existence of an optimal solution, we combine a dissipation inequality with an infinite-dimensional LaSalle invariance principle to prove strong convergence of every trajectory with a relatively compact positive orbit to the unique optimal state, control, and costate. Moreover, we present a sufficient condition for compactness through uniform control regularity and show that convergence holds for all initial states. Finally, we present an example with a strictly but not strongly convex running cost for which every mild solution converges strongly to the unique equilibrium, while no global exponential estimate uniformly over initial values can be obtained.
